name: Spite and Malice
description: Spite and Malice (also known as Cat and Mouse) is a competitive patience game for two or more players, traditionally played with two or more standard decks of cards. It is the direct ancestor of the commercial game Skip-Bo. The objective is to be the first to move all cards from your personal 'pay-off pile' onto center 'build piles'. Kings are wild (or Jokers), and Aces start the piles.
origin: United States (derived from Russian Bank / Crapette principles)

history.origins: Derived from Russian Bank (Crapette) principles but simpler. 'Spite' refers to blocking opponents.
timeline: 1900s: Included in Hoyle as 'Cat and Mouse'.
Present: Still played with standard cards by purists.
history.evolution: The use of Face Cards (J, Q, K) makes it slightly harder to read than numbered Skip-Bo cards.

setup.dealing: Shuffle both packs together. Deal 20 cards face down to each player's pay-off pile and 5 cards to each player's hand. Place the remainder face down as the stock. Turn the top card of each pay-off pile face up. The player with the higher pay-off card plays first (if equal, shuffle pay-off and turn a new top card).

rules.objective: Be the first to play all cards from your pay-off pile onto the center build stacks (ace through queen in sequence). Only the top card of your pay-off pile is playable at any time.
rules.gameplay: Shuffle both packs together. Each player has a face-down pay-off pile (20 cards) and a five-card hand; remainder is the stock. Turn order: player with higher pay-off top card plays first. On your turn, if you have fewer than five cards in hand, draw from stock to refill to five. You may then play cards to center stacks (ace to empty stack or next higher on existing, from hand, top of pay-off, or top of a side stack) or play one card from hand to one of your four side stacks, which ends your turn. Kings are wild. Max three center stacks; a completed stack (queen or king as queen) is shuffled into the stock by your opponent. You cannot play a pay-off card to a side stack or move cards between side stacks. If you play all five hand cards to the center without discarding, draw five more and continue.
keyRules: Center stacks: ace then 2 through queen; max three at a time.
Each player has up to four side stacks; playing to a side stack ends your turn.
Only the top card of pay-off and of each side stack is playable.

strategy.basic: Always check your Pay-off Pile card first. If it plays, play it. If not, check your hand/discards to see if you can make it play. Prioritize getting Pay-off cards out.
strategy.intermediate: Kings Usage: Save Kings for your Pay-off card. Don't waste a King to play a mundane card from your hand unless it unblocks your Pay-off.
strategy.advanced: Discard Stacking: Organize your 4 discard piles by rank (e.g., Pile 1 strict descending, Pile 2 trash). Don't bury useful cards. Watch opponent's Pay-off cardâ€”if they need a 7, and you have a 7, hold it.
tips: Keep an eye on the other player's top card.

variations.name: Unlimited center stacks
variations.description: Allow unlimited center stacks; completed stacks removed only when stock is depleted.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes only center stack limit; no engine constant overrides documented yet.

variations.name: Compulsory play of aces
variations.description: Aces must be played as soon as drawn or when on top of pay-off or side stack; no limit on number of center stacks.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds compulsory play rule; no engine overrides mapped for this variant yet.

variations.name: Scoring
variations.description: Winner scores 5 plus one per card left in opponent's pay-off pile; stalemate: score difference. Play to target (e.g. 50).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring variant would need targetScore and scoringDirection overrides; not yet added.
